external_submission.title: Evidence, Policy, and Settlement in Energy-Linked Financial Claims

research_question: Once external evidence is available, how should a financial decision distinguish what the evidence supports, whether a policy accepts it, how much underlying physical quantity it can justify before valuation, and whether the resulting obligation can settle?

prior_art_not_claimed_novel: oracle delivery of external data and oracle trust models
proof-of-reserve feeds and reserve-gated mint controls
research_positioning.bounded_contribution: An executable methodological composition that keeps source assurance, policy admission, supported physical quantity, and settlement as separately inspectable states under a fixed evidence object.
research_positioning.policy_status: researcher-declared comparison policies; not empirically calibrated, institutionally endorsed, or economically optimal
research_positioning.quantity_interpretation: 33.066 energy-claim units map one-for-one to the derived physical kWh surplus for this experiment; they are not a monetary price, market value, or legal entitlement
research_positioning.surplus_derivation: per interval max(PV generation - general load - controlled load, 0); derived surplus, not directly metered export

references: Eskandari et al. 2021, SoK: Oracles from the Ground Truth to Market Manipulation
W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0, 2025
Ratnam et al. 2017, Residential load and rooftop PV generation: an Australian distribution network dataset
